translationRepairs: Through repeated military achievements, he was promoted step by step to Biaoqi Commandant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu county.
Through repeated military achievements, he was promoted step by step to Biaoqi Commandant and enfeoffed as Count of Yufu county.
Chinese 縣伯 is a county earldom/countship (伯), not a marquisate (侯); 'Marquis' mistranslates 伯.
When Bozhi did rebel, the Emperor ordered a commandery in the province to accept Shan.
When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be placed in one commandery within the province.
Chinese 使反 means 'when the envoy/messenger returned', not 'when Bozhi rebelled'; context is the petition outcome before the open revolt announcement.
When he rebelled, Emperor Wu ordered one commandery within the province to take Shan in.
When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered one commandery within the province to accommodate Shan.
Same error as idiomatic: 使反 is the messenger's return, not Bozhi's rebellion.
His son Wuya was Direct Gate General. The Emperor wrote out Long Fu's crimes by hand, sealed the note, and sent it to Wuya, who opened it and showed his father.
Bozhi's son Wuya was then Direct Gate General. Emperor Wu personally wrote out Long Fu's crimes, sealed the note, and entrusted it to Wuya, who opened it and showed Bozhi.
Chinese is 直閤/直合將軍 and 武帝手疏...親付; English 'Direct Gate' is opaque and omits that Wu Di wrote and personally delivered the sealed charge.
Yun disliked Chi and firmly kept him out.
Yun disliked Chi and firmly refused him.
Chinese 堅拒之 is firm refusal of approaches, not merely keeping him out physically; minor clarity repair.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Linchuan, was ordered north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:
In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Linchuan, to invade the north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:
Source 詔…北侵 is an imperial order to invade; idiomatic softens to 'was ordered north' and omits the invasion sense.
In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan Hunchu to invade the north; Hunchu ordered his secretary Qiu Chi privately to write him a letter, saying:
In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan Hong to invade the north; Hong ordered his secretary Qiu Chi privately to write him a letter, saying:
Chinese 巨集 is a corrupted form of 宏 (Hong), personal name of the Prince of Linchuan; 'Hunchu' is not a valid reading.
In late spring, when Jiangnan's grass runs long and flowers speckle the trees, when parrots wheel in flocks—
In late spring, when Jiangnan's grass runs long and flowers speckle the trees, when orioles wheel in flocks—
Classic line is 群鶯亂飛 (orioles); packet Chinese 群鸚 is likely a corruption of 鶯, and 'parrots' mistranslates the famous phrasing.
At the end of spring, in the third month, grasses grow long in Jiangnan; mixed flowers bloom on trees, flocks of parrots fly in disorder.
At the end of spring, in the third month, grasses grow long in Jiangnan; mixed flowers bloom on trees, flocks of orioles fly in disorder.
Same 鸚/鶯 corruption: should be orioles (鶯), not parrots.
Your home still stands, your beloved wife still waits.
Your high hall has not fallen; your beloved concubine still lives.
Chinese 愛妾 is beloved concubine, not wife; 高堂未傾 is the high hall not collapsed.
Wei sent the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, with a hundred thousand men to oppose him.
Wei sent the Princes of Anfeng and Linhuai, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, with a hundred thousand men to oppose him.
Chinese 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huaihai.
He was transferred to the Eastern Palace's Direct Gate Guard.
He was transferred to Direct Gate (直閤) of the Eastern Palace.
Chinese 直合 is the common corruption of 直閤; 'Direct Gate Guard' is clearer as Direct Gate office.
In the first year of Datong, under Commander Cao Congzong he attacked Guoyang. Wei sent the Prince of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others to relieve it. Their vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li away.

In the first year of Datong, under Commander Cao Zhongzong he attacked Guoyang. Wei sent the Prince of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others to relieve it. Their vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li away.
Chinese 曹仲宗 is Zhongzong (仲宗); Congzong is a mistransliteration.

The Princes of Huaihai and Anfeng, Yu and Yanming, led the officials with the imperial carriage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace. He took the front hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

The Princes of Linhuai and Anfeng, Yu and Yanming, led the officials with the imperial carriage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace. He took the front hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
Chinese 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huaihai.

Once Hao had what he wanted, he sank into wine and women and neglected affairs. With the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai he plotted to betray Liang, but while the situation remained unsettled he still relied on Qingzhi's strength.

Once Hao had what he wanted, he sank into wine and women and neglected affairs. With the Princes of Anfeng and Linhuai he plotted to betray Liang, but while the situation remained unsettled he still relied on Qingzhi's strength.
Chinese 臨淮 is Linhuai; Huaihai is a mistranslation carried from earlier units.
Rong was about to withdraw when the astrologer Liu Lingzhu told him, "Within ten days Henan will be secured."
Rong was about to withdraw when the astrologer Liu Lingzhu (劉靈助) told him, "Within ten days Henan will be secured."
Confirming the Chinese personal name 劉靈助; English Liu Lingzhu is acceptable but the source characters should remain clear.
At his post Qingzhi besieged Xiangcheng and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.
At his post Qingzhi besieged Xianhu (縣瓠) and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.
Chinese 縣瓠 is Xianhu/Xiangcheng; confirm place rendering; Zhen River for 溱水 is acceptable.
His eldest son Zhaosi succeeded him.
His eldest son Zhao succeeded him.
Chinese 長子昭嗣 is often read as eldest son Zhao (昭) succeeded (嗣), not a compound given name Zhaosi.
When Ziyun later returned south, Lan Qin rose through battle honors in Liang's Tianjian era to Inspector of Jizhou.
When Ziyun later returned south, in Liang's Tianjian era he rose through battle honors to Inspector of Jizhou.
Chinese 後子雲還南，梁天監中以軍功至冀州刺史 attributes the Jizhou inspectorship to father Ziyun (cf. Liang Shu), not to Lan Qin.

I am forgotten in this world, broken and old. My means are those of Yan Hui or Yuan Xian; my name has never reached the great ministers. If I do not drink good wine every day, where else is there for me to go?

I am forgotten in this world, broken and old. My means are those of Yan and Yuan (顏原); my name has never reached the great ministers. If I do not drink good wine every day, where else is there for me to go?
Chinese 顏原 is the paired exemplars Yan Hui and Yuan Xian; the idiomatic expansion is acceptable but should stay clearly plural.
